title: The missing wallet
patientWords: You took my wallet. Give it back.
context: In the living room after returning from a clinic appointment.
behavior: Checking the same drawers repeatedly and watching me closely.
caregiverFeeling: Defensive and hurt that she did not trust me.

title: Refusing help with bathing
patientWords: Get out. I do not need you treating me like a baby.
context: In the bathroom after I laid out towels and turned on the shower.
behavior: Crossed his arms, raised his voice, and backed away from the shower.
caregiverFeeling: Embarrassed, frustrated, and worried he might slip.

title: Wanting to go home at sunset
patientWords: Take me home. My mother is waiting for me.
context: At home near sunset, just before dinner.
behavior: Standing by the front door with her handbag and checking the lock.
caregiverFeeling: Worried and sad that our home did not feel familiar.

title: Refusing a care task
patientWords: Stop ordering me around. You only want to control me.
context: At the kitchen table when I brought his scheduled medication.
behavior: Pushed the cup away and turned his chair from the table.
caregiverFeeling: Exhausted, angry, and afraid of doing the wrong thing.

title: Words of self-harm
patientWords: I am going to hurt myself. Leave me alone.
context: Late at night after a sudden and severe change in behavior.
behavior: Holding a sharp object and pushing away anyone who approaches.
caregiverFeeling: Frightened that she or someone else could be hurt.
